import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mtick
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the dataset
try:
    df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')
except FileNotFoundError:
    # Create a dummy dataframe for code execution if file is not found
    data = {'ID': [5524, 2174, 4141], 'Year_Birth': [1957, 1954, 1965], 'Education': ['Graduation', 'Graduation', 'PhD'], 'Marital_Status': ['Single', 'Single', 'Together'], 'Income': [58138.0, 46344.0, 71613.0], 'Kidhome': [0, 1, 0], 'Teenhome': [0, 1, 0], 'Dt_Customer': ['04-09-2012', '08-03-2014', '21-08-2013'], 'Recency': [58, 38, 26], 'MntWines': [635, 11, 426], 'MntFruits': [88, 1, 49], 'MntMeatProducts': [546, 6, 127], 'MntFishProducts': [172, 2, 111], 'MntSweetProducts': [88, 1, 21], 'MntGoldProds': [88, 6, 42], 'NumDealsPurchases': [3, 2, 1], 'NumWebPurchases': [8, 1, 8], 'NumCatalogPurchases': [10, 1, 2], 'NumStorePurchases': [4, 2, 10], 'NumWebVisitsMonth': [7, 5, 4], 'AcceptedCmp3': [0, 0, 0], 'AcceptedCmp4': [0, 0, 0], 'AcceptedCmp5': [0, 0, 0], 'AcceptedCmp1': [0, 0, 0], 'AcceptedCmp2': [0, 0, 0], 'Complain': [0, 0, 0], 'Z_CostContact': [3, 3, 3], 'Z_Revenue': [11, 11, 11], 'Response': [1, 0, 0]}
    df = pd.DataFrame(data)

# --- Data Preparation ---
# Feature Engineering: Create 'Age' and 'TotalSpending'
# Use the last customer enrollment year as the reference year for age calculation
df['Dt_Customer'] = pd.to_datetime(df['Dt_Customer'], dayfirst=True)
current_year = df['Dt_Customer'].dt.year.max()
df['Age'] = current_year - df['Year_Birth']

# Define spending columns and calculate total spending
spending_cols = ['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']
df['TotalSpending'] = df[spending_cols].sum(axis=1)

# Clean data: drop rows with missing income and filter extreme outliers for better visualization
df.dropna(subset=['Income'], inplace=True)
df = df[(df['Income'] < 200000) & (df['Age'] < 90)]

# Create 'AgeGroup' for segmentation
bins = [20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80]
labels = ['20s', '30s', '40s', '50s', '60s', '70s']
df['AgeGroup'] = pd.cut(df['Age'], bins=bins, labels=labels, right=False)

# --- Visualization ---
# Set theme and style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9))

# Create the scatter plot
# We use a subset of the data for the scatter plot to avoid overplotting and make the viz clearer
plot_df = df.sample(n=min(1000, len(df)), random_state=42)

scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=plot_df,
    x='Income',
    y='TotalSpending',
    hue='AgeGroup',
    size='TotalSpending',
    sizes=(20, 250),
    palette='viridis',
    alpha=0.7,
    edgecolor='black',
    linewidth=0.5,
    ax=ax
)

# --- Annotations and Styling ---
# Set titles and labels
ax.set_title('Customer Spending Power: Income vs. Total Spending by Age Group', fontsize=18, weight='bold', pad=20)
ax.set_xlabel('Annual Household Income', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Total Spending (Last 2 Years)', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)

# Format axis ticks
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mtick.FuncFormatter(lambda x, _: f'${x/1000:.0f}K'))
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mtick.FuncFormatter(lambda x, _: f'${x/1000:.0f}K'))
plt.xticks(fontsize=12)
plt.yticks(fontsize=12)

# Customize the legend
handles, labels = scatter.get_legend_handles_labels()
# Separate hue and size legends
hue_legend_labels = labels[1:len(df['AgeGroup'].unique())+1]
hue_legend_handles = handles[1:len(df['AgeGroup'].unique())+1]
size_legend_labels = labels[len(df['AgeGroup'].unique())+2:]
size_legend_handles = handles[len(df['AgeGroup'].unique())+2:]

# Create two separate legends
legend1 = ax.legend(hue_legend_handles, hue_legend_labels, title='Age Group', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', fontsize=11, title_fontsize=13)
legend2 = ax.legend(size_legend_handles, size_legend_labels, title='Total Spending', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.6), loc='upper left', fontsize=11, title_fontsize=13, labelspacing=1.2)
ax.add_artist(legend1) # Add the first legend back to the plot

# Add a regression line to show the overall trend
sns.regplot(
    data=df,
    x='Income',
    y='TotalSpending',
    scatter=False,
    color='#e74c3c',
    line_kws={'linestyle':'--', 'linewidth':2},
    ax=ax
)
# Add a custom entry for the regression line in the legend area
ax.text(1.03, 0.45, 'Overall Trend', transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=12, color='#e74c3c', weight='bold')

# Add an insightful annotation
ax.annotate(
    'High-Income, High-Spending Segment',
    xy=(90000, 2000),
    xytext=(110000, 2200),
    arrowprops=dict(facecolor='black', shrink=0.05, width=1, headwidth=8),
    fontsize=12,
    bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.3", fc="ivory", ec="black", lw=1)
)

# Despine for a cleaner look
sns.despine(trim=True)
fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 1]) # Adjust layout to make space for legends

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
